description: Structured companion to label_error_crossref.md -- the pair-by-pair cross-reference of this project's flagged near-neighbor pairs against mnist_lipschitz/data/known_label_errors_mnist_test.json. Indices recovered from already-saved near-neighbor search results (mnist_experiment_arrays.npz, stronger_cnn_raw_mnist_arrays.npz). REVISED from the original version of this file: the original-CNN/logistic-regression rows previously listed pairs ('8/2', '8/0', '0/7') that turned out to be stale -- generated under an earlier default of run_mnist_experiment's n_lipschitz_points parameter (300, before commit 48bd088 changed it to 1000). Rows below reflect the current, reproducible top-6 Euclidean near-neighbor pairs for each of the three original models. See root_cause_of_prior_mismatch below for the full diagnosis.
conclusion: Of all 22 checked pairs across all four model/run groups, only one involves a known label error: the original CNN's current rank-3 pair (test index 9679). Every other pair -- including all of logistic regression's top pairs, which are almost entirely same-digit '1/1' pairs -- is clean, supporting genuine model behavior over labeling artifacts as the general pattern, with one confirmed exception.

root_cause_of_prior_mismatch.summary: The original CNN's '8/2'/'8/0' pairs and logistic regression's '0/7' (previously documented in this notebook's 'Highest-ratio near-neighbour pairs' section) were generated when run_mnist_experiment's n_lipschitz_points defaulted to 300 (commit 4db5ae9, 2026-08-12). Commit 48bd088, the very next day (2026-08-13, 'Add covariance eigenvalue spectrum plot to mnist_lipschitz'), changed that default to 1000. n_lipschitz_points sizes query_idx (the Lipschitz-estimator query set), which is passed as exclude_idx to the ratio-distribution analysis's stratified near-neighbor subset draw -- so even with an identical seed, a different exclude_idx produces a different subset, hence different near-neighbor pairs. Model training itself is unaffected and remains bit-for-bit reproducible (accuracy numbers from reruns during this investigation matched README.md's documented table exactly to 4 decimal places) -- only the near-neighbor subset composition shifted. Confirmed via git log -S on run_experiment.py and cross-checked by rerunning run_mnist_experiment() with current code, seed=0: results matched the currently-saved results/mnist_experiment_arrays.npz exactly, not the notebook's old prose. This is genuine stale documentation from an earlier code state, not file corruption or non-determinism.
